summary: Iteration-8: verified all three fixes for VIRTUE 3D FPS. Fix #1 (Spectate POV) — spectate WS welcome payload exposes spectator=true + spectate_target_id; engine.js (1578-1612) sets weapon slot via t.weapon mapping + hides target mesh via visibility skip at line 1723; viewmodel-visible gate at 1970 keeps gun rendered for locked spectator. Fix #2 (Party ranked queue follower POV) — POST /api/queue/ranked by leader makes GET /api/queue/ranked by follower return in_queue=true with the same tier, is_party=true, party_size=2 (consumed by QueueContext 3s background poll → PartyPanel data-testid=party-member-queue-info). Fix #3 (Party ranked match start, shared bot room) — after bot-fill, both leader AND follower observe matched=true with the same match_id; both ranked WS connections resolve to the SAME ranked_bot_room (room.players includes both real users) via shared room_key stamped on MATCHED_USERS at matchmaker_loop line 2913 and read by WS handler line 3806. 8/8 pytest passing including the cross-WS room-sharing test that proves the leader sees the follower in their state frames after both connect with mode=ranked.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2911-2913 matchmaker_loop bot-fill correctly stamps shared_key=a_uids[0] (leader's user_id) onto every party member's MATCHED_USERS entry. Solo bot-fills get shared_key=their own uid via the same code path — backward compatible.

server.py:3801-3807 WS ranked handler reads matched.get('room_key') or u_id, so followers resolve to the leader's GameRoom and the GameRoom instance is shared (get_or_create_ranked_bot_room returns existing room for the same key). Confirmed via live WS test: leader's state frames contain the follower's username after they both connect.

server.py:3837-3839 spectate ranked branch uses loc.get('ranked_bot_key') to find ranked-bot rooms regardless of whether the spectated user is the room key holder — correct given the new shared-room model.

server.py:3093-3110 GET /api/queue/ranked surfaces is_party + party_size from the queue entry's user_ids list — so QueueContext's background poll on the follower's tab sees the same in_queue payload the leader sees (verified live: party of 2 leader+player2, follower GET returns in_queue=true is_party=true party_size=2).

engine.js:1590-1597 weapon-slot mapping (ak47→primary, katana→secondary, laser→tertiary) is correct and idempotent (only calls setWeapon when slot actually changes). t.laser_firing mirror at 1599 keeps remote-beam fx accurate. Hiding target mesh via visibility loop at 1604-1610 + the persistent skip at 1723-1725 prevents both the initial helmet clip AND any per-state-frame override that would re-show the body.
engine.js:1970-1973 keeps weapon viewmodel visible when isSpectator && spectateTargetId, hidden when just spectating without a target — clean gating.

QueueContext.jsx:138-157 background 3s poll (bgPollIdRef) correctly skips while active poll is running OR during the match-found countdown to avoid double-firing the navigation. Initial tick() on mount means the timer surfaces within milliseconds of the leader queuing, not 3s later.

QueueContext.jsx:88-93 navigation dispatches the 'virtue-match-loading' CustomEvent + nav('/play?mode=ranked') AFTER the 3-2-1 countdown completes — same path for leader and follower so the experience is identical.

Minor: server.py spectate route returns 4404 → handshake HTTP 403 when target user isn't in DB (e.g., bots). The problem statement's suggestion to '/spectate/<bot_username>' won't actually work via WS because _find_user_by_username queries db.users only. Recommend extending it to also check active room player usernames for bots — optional enhancement, not a regression.

success_rate.backend: 100% (8/8) — 2 spectate WS welcome+rejection, 2 party-follower queue status, 2 party bot-fill shared room (matched same id + same WS room confirmed via cross-state observation), 2 smoke
success_rate.frontend: Lobby renders cleanly after login (player1 LV5, 950 coins, BRONZE 0 RP); spectate route renders SPECTATING banner + HUD chrome (FPS/PING/AMMO/EXIT); WS for spectating an offline user correctly fails handshake (403) so the SPECTATING banner shows DISCONNECTED state — expected. Party UI testids (party-member-queue-info / party-waiting) live behind party state which the single-tab smoke test can't form.

test_credentials: player1@shooter.com / player123 (already L5). player2@shooter.com / player123 — bumped stats.bonus_xp=5000 directly in MongoDB so player2 hit L6 and clears RANKED_MIN_LEVEL=5. Friendship player1↔player2 already established by iteration-6.
seed_data_creation: Set player2 stats.bonus_xp=5000 (idempotent — re-running tests is fine). Friendship + party state are cleaned up before/after each test by fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: `python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8_party_ranked_spectate.py -v -c /app/backend/tests/pytest.ini --tb=short --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/iteration8_results.xml`. Bronze tier bot-fill takes ~10-15s, so the two TestPartyRankedBotFillSharedRoom tests each spend ~15-60s waiting — the full suite runs in ~110s. The cross-WS shared-room test drains 8s of state frames per socket to let the late joiner appear in the other side's state — if you tighten that window the test can flake. Spectating bots via /spectate/<bot_username> won't work because _find_user_by_username queries db.users only; spectate tests use a real user (player2 joining casual). If player2 ever drops below L5 again, re-bump via `db.users.update_one({'email':'player2@shooter.com'},{'$set':{'stats.bonus_xp':5000}})`.
rca of the issue: N/A — all three fixes verified end-to-end. The critical assertion was that BOTH party members' ranked WS connections land in the SAME ranked_bot_room (proven by leader's state frames containing the follower's username), which directly validates the shared room_key flow added at server.py:2913 + 3806.
